channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Packers signed WR Kaden Prather, formerly of the Bills.
item.description: Prather caught nine passes for 148 yards for the UFL’s Louisville Kings during the 2026 season. He spent the 2025 season as a practice squad player for the Bills.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports that Giants WR Malik Nabers (knee) said he has been running routes for “weeks” and that his reported clean-up procedure date was incorrect.
item.description: Well, that could explain a lot. Nabers shocked many of us by showing off fairly crisp route running at training camp this week. A week ago, he was thought to be a candidate for the PUP list. Back in May, news broke that Nabers had undergone a clean-up procedure on his knee “multiple weeks ago.” Although ambiguous, it was apparently incorrect. Nabers did not specify in which direction, but given his participation, one assumes the procedure occurred earlier than the report indicated. Positive reports continue to roll in for the young star.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that the Chiefs are catering to RB Kenneth Walker’s formation preferences and featuring him in the screen game.
item.description: Taylor reported early in June that the Chiefs were “starting to experiment” with what works best with Walker’s skills. The veteran back prefers plays from under center rather than shotgun formation. Now that the Chiefs’ training camp is underway, we can confirm that they are putting his preferences into practice. More than half of the Chiefs’ snaps in the first team period came from under center, allowing Walker to practice running between the tackles under coach Andy Reid’s watchful eye. The Chiefs also continue to give Walker reps in the screen game, which can help keep Walker involved in the passing game, regardless of his development as a receiver and pass protector this offseason. Impressed with Walker’s screen game chops thus far, Chiefs C Creed Humphrey described Walker as “a dynamic player, a freak athlete and great with his reads.” Walker is a fantasy football RB1 who could surprise some this season.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes focused on taking snaps under center and working on play action on Thursday.
item.description: This is notable because Mahomes used shotgun formation on 80.6 percent of snaps last season, the third-highest in the league per Taylor, and the Chiefs’ 22.6 percent play-action rate ranked just 26th. NFL offenses averaged 7.76 yards per pass play with play action and 6.65 without it last year. Upping the play-action rate would be great for fantasy purposes.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Colts hosted free agent WR Chase Claypool for a workout on Thursday.
item.description: Claypool has not played since the 2023 season. Were he to sign with the Colts, he would not meaningfully impact the incumbent players’ target shares.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Saints signed WR Chris Olave to a four-year, $132 million extension through 2030.
item.description: The deal includes $90 million guaranteed. Olave, 26, ranked sixth in the NFL with 151 targets last year despite missing Week 18 due to blood clots in his lungs. He spent the offseason recovering and, aside from holding in yesterday, participating as much as possible. He was cleared to fully practice on Tuesday. He is a fantasy football WR1, playing in an ascending Saints offense.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars RB Bhayshul Tuten’s “terrific practice performances” have been a consistent part of spring practices and training camp.
item.description: Shipley acknowledges that he keeps writing about how good Tuten has looked, but he reasonably counters that he can only report what he’s seeing. Evidently, he’s seeing Tuten “building a lot of momentum” while RB Chris Rodriguez (foot) is stuck in individual drills. Drafting players in ambiguous backfields has been an established, sharp strategy for years now. Although this bunch could be losing its ambiguity a tad, Tuten’s Rounds 5-6 best ball ADP could still end up being a bargain.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Bears WR Rome Odunze said his foot “feels amazing.”
item.description: Odunze caused concern earlier this offseason, saying his 2025 foot injury created “a different type of foot structure” and that he was learning to deal with the “new normal.” Speaking with ESPN’s Courtney Cronin today, Odunze said he articulated his prior comments poorly and that his foot issue is “not even really something that I think about anymore.” Sounds like he has successfully adjusted to the new normal, which is great to hear. Odunze is jockeying for position in the Bears’ target pecking order with TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden this summer.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Seahawks activated DT Deven Eastern off the physically unable to perform list.
item.description: The seventh-round rookie is back on the Seahawks roster after missing most of organized team activities and mandatory minicamp. He will now compete for a roster spot.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
item.description: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.-Nic Bodiford
